data.title: Collapsed floors prevent investigators reaching heart of Khlongthom fire
data.description: Police investigators on Monday could not reach the point of origin amid the debris of the fire that destroyed the Klongthom Centre in Bangkok last week because two upper floors had collapsed on top of it. Arson has still not been ruled out.

data.title: US carrier visit to Thailand's Pattaya lifts hope and sex-tourism risk
data.description: After a long deployment in the Middle East, a US Navy aircraft carrier will dock in Thailand's resort city of Pattaya this week, raising hopes of an economic boost, even as local authorities cracked down on parts of the sex tourism destination.

data.title: Govt identifiies 767 factories operating unlawfully
data.description: The government has identified 767 factories operating illegally nationwide, but mostly in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC), with 131 already shutdown.

data.title: Pattaya bar shooting leaves two wounded
data.description: CHON BURI - A late-night dispute between two men in a Pattaya bar escalated into gunfire in the early hours of Monday, leaving both men wounded in the street after three shots were fired.

data.title: Persistent rain closes waterfalls in Saraburi
data.description: SARABURI - Persistent rain has swollen waterways in Saraburi, leading to the closure of two waterfalls, in Kaeng Khoi and Muak Lek districts, affecting several villages, resorts and tourist access.

data.title: Poll backs 3rd phase of subsidy scheme
data.description: Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has welcomed strong support for the government's "Thais Help Thais Plus" subsidy programme, which was named its top achievement in a Suan Dusit Poll this month.

data.title: How the 'Blue Senators' claim turned into a sprawling probe
data.description: <p>In late July, Internet Dialogue on Law Reform (iLaw) Director Yingcheep Atchanont presented evidence alleging that nine Bhumjaithai Party (BJT) figures, including party leader and Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, manipulated the 2024 Senate election.</p>

data.title: Excise tax for car industry set for review
data.description: <p>The government is accelerating an overhaul of the excise tax structure to retain investment in Thailand's automotive industry, particularly as the electric vehicle market expands, government spokeswoman Rachada Dhnadirek said on Sunday.</p>

data.title: MoU to boost Ethopia ties
data.description: Thailand and Ethiopia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) establishing a mechanism for regular political consultations and exchanges on regional and international issues of mutual interest.

data.title: Senior officers benched after club raid
data.description: <p>Five senior police officers from Huai Khwang district have been transferred to an inactive post following a raid on a suspected unlicensed entertainment venue in the area.</p>

data.title: Cops arrest American man wanted for child sex abuse
data.description: <p>Phuket: An American man wanted in the United States on eight warrants over alleged sexual offences against children was arrested at a hotel on Saturday, police said.</p>

data.title: Money and politics blamed for unrest
data.description: Residents of the three southern border provinces point to budget allocations, grey-capital interests and local politics as leading factors behind the latest wave of unrest, a Nida Poll survey found.

data.title: Poll backs 3rd phase of subsidy scheme
data.description: Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has welcomed strong support for the government's "Thais Help Thais Plus" subsidy programme, which was named its top achievement in a Suan Dusit Poll this month.

data.title: EC denies narrowing Senate charges to 10
data.description: <p>The Election Commission (EC) on Sunday dismissed speculation it had already decided to charge only 10 people in the Senate election collusion case.</p>

data.title: How the 'Blue Senators' claim turned into a sprawling probe
data.description: <p>In late July, Internet Dialogue on Law Reform (iLaw) Director Yingcheep Atchanont presented evidence alleging that nine Bhumjaithai Party (BJT) figures, including party leader and Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, manipulated the 2024 Senate election.</p>

data.title: Aussies seek broader ties
data.description: <p>Australia is seeking a broader and more resilient partnership with Thailand, with new ambassador Pablo Kang identifying trade and supply chains, artificial intelligence, transnational crime, clean energy and Thailand's OECD ambitions as key areas for deeper cooperation.</p>

data.title: Minister calls for action to curb coastal erosion
data.description: <p>SONGKHLA: Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn has ordered state agencies to accelerate measures to curb coastal erosion in Thepha district, warning the problem could pose a risk to Highway 43, a key route to Thailand's southern border provinces.</p>

data.title: Forensics due today at Khlong Thom site
data.description: <p>More than 100 witnesses and victims have been questioned as police investigate the fire at Bangkok's Khlong Thom Center, with forensic examination of the site expected to begin at 8am on Monday.</p>

data.title: The paradox of Anutin's govt
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's government may have little to fear from a parliamentary revolt, but its biggest political threat could be building beyond the walls of parliament: a growing public perception that corruption, political collusion and double standards are becoming entrenched under its watch.</p>

data.title: No evidence yet of arson in Klongthom Centre fire
data.description: Police have so far found no evidence of arson in the Klongthom Shopping Centre fire to support speculation of a conspiracy to force some businesses out, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Sunday.

data.title: Pattaya street hookers arrested ahead of US carrier group's visit
data.description: PATTAYA - Police and human security officials arrested Thai, Lao and Ugandan women for alleged street prostitution on Saturday night, oonly days ahead of the arrival of about 5,000 crew and marines aboard a US navy strike group.

data.title: Man arrested for B5m bomb-assisted gold robbery
data.description: SA KAEO - A suspect was arrested at his home in Aranyaprathet district on Sunday after a local gold shop was bombed and robbed of gold necklaces worth about 5 million baht on Thursday.

data.title: PM attributes continuing southern violence to intensified law enforcement
data.description: The continuing criminal violence in the southern border provinces is a response to intensified enforcement of the law, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Sunday.

data.title: Van driver caught with 4m meth pills
data.description: AMNAT CHAROEN - Police seized 4 million methamphetamine pills worth an estimated 200 million baht and arrested a van driver following a late-night chase in this northeastern province.

data.title: Man with knife arrested at school earlier drank pig's blood and beer
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA - Police were called to arrest a man who was acting weirdly in a school yard after earlier drinking pig's blood and beer, in Khon Buri district.

data.title: Gunmen storm Pattani department store, set off bombs
data.description: PATTANI - Armed insurgents stormed into a big department store in Pattani on Saturday evening, forcing customers and employees to leave before detonating three bombs.
